precepts.text: Evil men understand not judgment: but they that seek the Lord understand all things. That is why some are always confused when leadership passes a judgment: they do not know the scriptures, so they do not understand the sentence of judgment.
precepts.point: This chapter deals with the man whose whole occupation is his worldly craft. Without these cannot a city be inhabited; the work is needed. But they shall not be sought for in public counsel, nor sit high in the congregation, nor sit on the judges' seat, nor understand the sentence of judgment. If all you know is your job and not the scriptures, why would you be asked anything in counsel?

note.label: Recovering the Remnant: Worldwide Blitz

precepts.why:
Sirach says the man whose whole occupation is his worldly job shall not “understand the sentence of judgment”. Why don't you understand when judgments are passed? Proverbs answers: “Evil men understand not judgment: but they that seek the Lord understand all things.”

That is the brother who is always confused. When leadership makes a judgment, he doesn't agree, even if he disagrees in silence. You don't agree because you don't know the scriptures. All you know is your job, not the word of God, so you are always confused. And the Bible says you are evil.

So that brother “shall not be sought for in publick counsel”. When things are going down, we don't want to hear your opinion, because your opinion is your work, your job. He will not “sit high in the congregation” or have rank, and he will not “be found where parables are spoken”, because he could care less. If the shoe fits, brother, wear it. If you want to be a member, be a member; there is nothing wrong with that.

But they that seek the Lord understand all things. Chapter 39 shows the flip side: the one that “giveth his mind to the law of the most High”. He seeks out the wisdom of the ancients, is found where the subtle parables are, and he shall serve among great men and appear before princes.

precepts.text: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins. That goes all the way back to Leviticus: when you brought your sacrifice before the priest, that was a public confession; you walked through the midst of all Israel with your offering. Today we hide behind walls and technology and think nobody knows; the Lord sees right through it.
precepts.point: He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: when you try to cover that bitterness, the roots keep growing; you are just hauling in more soil to dump on top of the stump. But whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy: that is what we all want.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
“He that covereth his sins shall not prosper”: when you try to cover that bitterness, the roots keep growing, and you are just bringing in dump trucks to load more soil on top of it. But whoso confesses shall have mercy, and John shows why: “If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins”. The Lord is faithful and just when we confess our sins.

That goes all the way back to Leviticus. When you brought your sacrifice before the priest, that was a public confession. You had to walk through the midst of all Israel with your offering.

Now we have the white man, his walls and his technology. We have VPNs: yeah, don't nobody know I'm on OnlyFans, I got a VPN, I'm broadcasting from the Philippines. No, brother, the Lord sees right through it.

So in order to get over the root of bitterness we have to confess it: damn, I had the devil on me. Covering it will never prosper; confessing it is how we get the mercy we all want.

precepts.text: Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. We should be comfortable confessing our faults, because no temptation has taken you but such as is common to man. You confess to a brother and he says, brother, I was dealing with the same spirit, and you feel a lot better. Everybody deals with a level of bitterness, of lust, of lack of faith. That is not getting on the public announcement; it is finding a godly man and saying, I have this going on, I need help. They are going to help you.
precepts.point: He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: when you try to cover that bitterness, the roots keep growing; you are just hauling in more soil to dump on top of the stump. But whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy: that is what we all want.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Confessing is not only to the Lord. James says: “Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.”

We should be comfortable confessing our faults, because, as 1 Corinthians 10:13 says, no temptation has taken you but such as is common to man. You confess your fault, and a brother might say, brother, I was dealing with the same spirit. Woo, man, I feel a lot better. All of this is common. We all have levels of bitterness; some have a higher degree than others, but everybody deals with a level of bitterness, a level of lust, a level of lack of faith.

That doesn't mean getting on the public announcement. It means you see a godly man and say, hey Cap, hey D, I have this going on, I need help with it. They are going to help you. They are not going to say, brother, you got the devil on you, get away from me. It is Satan telling us otherwise.

That is whoso confesseth and forsaketh: confessing to the Lord, confessing one to another, and being healed, instead of covering the sin and letting the root grow.

precepts.text: A man that doeth violence to the blood of any person shall flee to the pit; let no man stay him; do not hide sin among Israel, bring it out.
precepts.point: A lot of people do not know how to apply this verse; the precept for Leviticus 5:1 is Deuteronomy 17:4. Whether the thing be told thee or thou hast heard of it, thou shalt enquire diligently, and only when it be true and the thing certain does judgment proceed: make sure you are certain of a thing before you bring somebody to judgment.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
“A man that doeth violence to the blood of any person shall flee to the pit; let no man stay him.”

Let no man stay him: do not hide sin among Israel, bring it out. The witness who has seen or known of it and does not utter it is staying the guilty man, and he shall bear his iniquity.

precepts.text: He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool; following your own mind instead of the scripture is folly.
precepts.point: From the beginning the Most High commanded the prophets to speak his words and diminish not a word: do not be afraid to tell the nations what the scripture actually says, that salvation is to Israel and that there is no female deity.

note.label: Deuteronomy 4: Neither Add nor Diminish

precepts.why:
“He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool: but whoso walketh wisely, he shall be delivered.” Following your own mind instead of the scripture is folly.

An opinion off the top of your head cannot be proven by scripture, and the man who trusts that heart and adds it to the word is a fool. Whoso walks wisely, by the word as it was commanded, neither adding nor diminishing, shall be delivered.

precepts.text: He that covereth his sins shall not prosper, but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy; hide your sins and you will be buried by them.
precepts.point: Prayer is largely invalid if there is no action behind it. If you ask for a home but take no steps toward the finances, why would you receive it. Faith without works is dead.

note.label: Psalm 30: Joy Cometh in the Morning

precepts.why:
David asks “What profit is there in my blood, when I go down to the pit? Shall the dust praise thee?” and then “Hear, O Lord, and have mercy upon me: Lord, be thou my helper.” Solomon shows how that mercy comes: “He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.” Hide your sins and you will be buried by them.

That is why repenting daily means naming the sin specifically. The Most High looks for us to say exactly what we are dealing with. One brother may struggle with fornication, another with cigarettes; you cannot bring the same prayer for both, so make it clearly known what you are dealing with, the way you would tell your mother or father exactly what you need, not just asking the Lord to bless you. Confess it, then forsake it, and the mercy David prayed for comes.

precepts.text: He that covereth his sins shall not prosper, but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy, so repentance is confessing and forsaking, with counsel.
precepts.point: Lord, I have hoped for Thy salvation, and done Thy commandments. My soul hath kept Thy testimonies, and I love them exceedingly. I have kept Thy precepts and Thy testimonies, for all my ways are before Thee.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.” Repentance is confessing and forsaking, with counsel; we seek counsel from leadership rather than covering our sins.

That is how we offend less in the things we are battling, part of our pilgrimage toward the great peace of them that love the law. David lived that way: “My soul hath kept thy testimonies; and I love them exceedingly. I have kept thy precepts and thy testimonies: for all my ways are before thee.” Nothing was covered; all his ways were before the Most High.

precepts.text: Seeing the boldness of Peter and John, unlearned men, they took knowledge that they had been with Jesus.
precepts.point: For the transgression of a land many are its princes, but by a man of understanding and knowledge its state shall be prolonged. That understanding and knowledge is the Most High's commandments; David told Solomon that keeping the commandments keeps a man on the throne of Israel.

note.label: Proverbs 28: The Righteous Are Bold as a Lion

precepts.why:
“The wicked flee when no man pursueth: but the righteous are bold as a lion.” Peter and John show that boldness: “Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled; and they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.”

They were perceived as unlearned men, yet their boldness made men take knowledge that they had been with Christ, who taught as one having authority. The boldness came from being with him.

We can be bold this same way by using the words of the Most High, which no one can gainsay. That is the righteous bold as a lion: not learning or standing, but the words of the Most High in the mouth.

precepts.text: Keep the charge of the Most High and walk in his ways, and if your children take heed there shall not fail you a man on the throne of Israel.
precepts.point: For the transgression of a land many are its princes, but by a man of understanding and knowledge its state shall be prolonged. That understanding and knowledge is the Most High's commandments; David told Solomon that keeping the commandments keeps a man on the throne of Israel.

note.label: Proverbs 28: The Righteous Are Bold as a Lion

precepts.why:
“For the transgression of a land many are the princes thereof: but by a man of understanding and knowledge the state thereof shall be prolonged.” That understanding and knowledge is the Most High's commandments.

David told Solomon the same when he charged him: “be thou strong therefore, and shew thyself a man; And keep the charge of the Lord thy God, to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, and his commandments, and his judgments, and his testimonies, as it is written in the law of Moses, that thou mayest prosper in all that thou doest, and whithersoever thou turnest thyself”. And the promise tied to it: “If thy children take heed to their way, to walk before me in truth with all their heart and with all their soul, there shall not fail thee (said he) a man on the throne of Israel.”

Keeping the commandments keeps a man on the throne of Israel. That is the man of understanding and knowledge by whom the state of the land is prolonged; transgression multiplies princes, but the commandments keep the throne.

precepts.text: The Most High hears not sinners, but the worshipper that does his will.
precepts.point: He that turns away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be an abomination, as John 9 says the Most High does not hear sinners.

note.label: Proverbs 28: The Righteous Are Bold as a Lion

precepts.why:
“He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be abomination.” Turn your ear from the law and even your prayer is an abomination.

John 9 says the same: “Now we know that God heareth not sinners: but if any man be a worshipper of God, and doeth his will, him he heareth.” The Most High does not hear sinners; he hears the worshipper that does his will. The man who will not hear the law is the sinner whose prayer goes unheard.

So keeping the law is not separate from prayer. The wise son who keeps the law is the one whose prayer is heard.

precepts.text: Do not turn your face or eye from the afflicted and needy, lest they curse you and be heard.
precepts.point: When the wicked rise, men hide themselves, but when they perish the righteous increase.

note.label: Proverbs 28: The Righteous Are Bold as a Lion

precepts.why:
“He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack: but he that hideth his eyes shall have many a curse.” Ecclesiasticus says the same: “Reject not the supplication of the afflicted; neither turn away thy face from a poor man. Turn not away thine eye from the needy, and give him none occasion to curse thee”.

Do not turn your face or your eye from the afflicted and the needy, for if he curses you in the bitterness of his soul, his prayer is heard. That is the many a curse that comes on the man who hides his eyes.

Sirach 12 says if you do good, know to whom you do it, and the law commands us to help our brothers who keep the commandments. Give to the poor among your brothers and you shall not lack; hide your eyes and the curse is heard.

precepts.text: Do not harden your heart or shut your hand from your poor brother, but open your hand wide and lend him sufficient for his need.
precepts.point: When the wicked rise, men hide themselves, but when they perish the righteous increase.

note.label: Proverbs 28: The Righteous Are Bold as a Lion

precepts.why:
“He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack: but he that hideth his eyes shall have many a curse.” The law commands it: “If there be among you a poor man of one of thy brethren within any of thy gates in thy land which the Lord thy God giveth thee, thou shalt not harden thine heart, nor shut thine hand from thy poor brother: But thou shalt open thine hand wide unto him, and shalt surely lend him sufficient for his need, in that which he wanteth.”

Do not harden your heart or shut your hand from your poor brother; open your hand wide and lend him sufficient for his need. The one hiding his eyes in Proverbs is the one hardening his heart and shutting his hand here.

The law commands us to help our brothers who keep the commandments, and Sirach 12 says if you do good, know to whom you do it. If your poor brother curses you in the bitterness of his soul, his prayer is heard; open your hand and you shall not lack.

points: The atonement is a time of self-reflection. Once a year you examine your sins, what you've done. Some of you battling hatred, anger, fornication, jealousy, envy. Bitterness, that's a big one in here.
You can't hide those things. They eventually leak out of you over time. They corrupt you.
An author mentioned three Fs, and it's not my quote: whatever you choose not to let go, it festers, it ferments, and it becomes fragmented.
Fester: for a negative feeling or a bad situation to grow worse over time because it is ignored. It grows, it spreads, and you refuse to acknowledge it.

Ferment: to be in a state of agitation; turmoil, unrest, upheaval. First it festers, then you undergo change. You see it in the person's face, their countenance changes, they act different, they speak different, they isolate themselves. At that point you and Satan are best friends. Everybody becomes the bad guy, and only you see the spirit.
But whoso confesseth: if you got a problem, you speak on it. You don't want to speak on it, it will fester, and it will ferment.
Fragment: a small piece that has broken off, or separated from a whole.

points: He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy. If you cover your sins or make excuses for them, or reason as to why it is okay or acceptable, then you will not be forgiven. But if you confess your sins and are honest and come forth, then the Lord will have mercy on you.

Remember what Samuel just said: if I did anything to anybody, I will restore it to them. Show me where, so I can restore it, if anybody can say it. But if you try to hide behind your things, and do not take accountability.

In the past, what happened here: I spoke to the brother, he acknowledged what he was wrong in, he said he did it. I had him call leadership and speak to three or four of the leadership. And after we hung up I told him, if you say anything other than what you just admitted to, we have witnesses, and Satan has entered into your heart. The next day he said, I did not do it. I said, God, you are the devil. I could not believe it. Well, no, of course I could believe it. But the point was, from the time that he acknowledged it, I said, okay, good. Twenty-four hours later, that is not what happened. How could people follow that? Impossible. You would destroy what is being built. You are moving as an antichrist. You are moving against God's kingdom and building it back.

So, leadership principles. Transparency does not require exposing every private matter, but it does require honesty concerning matters that affect the people. We have to bring it out. We cannot brush it underneath the rug. It cannot be private. That is the way the people gain trust in the congregation. If you want the people to trust you, you have to be willing to listen to the people, hear matters out. That is why I told you we hear things, and because we do not move right away, do not think that we are not paying attention. Do not think we are not going to do anything. But there are certain systems in place, the way we have to do it, and allow it to play itself out. And that is why you see us here now, because we do care. It is important to us that we watch Sack grow and recover.
